cells.tense: The release is happening on time and nothing gets ahead of you now.
cells.act: learn how it grows by tending it
cells.ask: Take a living thing you're part of — a plant, a crew, a project — and for a while give it what it asks for and nothing extra. Follow the pace it keeps rather than the one you'd set.
cells.core:
Something in your hands is being carried, and you know how it moves. You take the next step without seeing the whole road, and the steps keep landing under you. The direction belongs to you and so do the hands, and the half-light is not a problem here — it's the condition that lets you move without forcing what you can't see yet.

What is still growing gets tended without being rushed. Notice how it grows and work with that instead of on it. Ambiguity stops being something to solve, because here you only ever need the next step, not the whole map, and you're taking it.
cells.sheetLine: You carry it and you set it down on time.
cells.verb: directing what gets carried and what gets set down
cells.place: in the half-light where the road only shows the next step

cells.tense: The future is a map you keep redrawing and that no step can fit into.
cells.act: write the facts down in order, without feeling words
cells.ask: Write what's actually here, in plain order, no feeling words and no plans for it. Read the page back before any decision bigger than the day.
cells.core:
You can normally move through fog, and lately the fog is where you live. You've been bracing against a future you can't write yet, filling the blank with scenarios, plans, outcomes, so the half-light every step would come from hasn't arrived. Whole days go to rehearsing states that haven't happened. Uncertainty has become the thing you're managing, not the road you're on.

Less of the fog, more of what's here. Put down the plain facts in order and keep the page dull. It will be shorter than you fear, and the next step will be visible in a way it hasn't been all week.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you already.
cells.act: lay the one step you can see, solidly
cells.ask: Take whatever's nearest and real — a form, a shelf, a step. Do it through to its end, then stop and look at it done before you move.
cells.core:
You're carrying a decision already made, holding on as though it hadn't happened yet. The whole road has closed into a single unfinished door, and presence is somewhere else, waiting for permission to move on. Nothing in the fog is reachable right now — only what's directly in your hands.

Don't try to release all of it yet. Put down a step that's visible and real, and stand it up solidly where you can see it. The quiet after won't come from a decision, but from doing the thing your hands already have. The next step will show itself from inside the work.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding a door that's already closed.
cells.verb: directing what gets carried and what gets set down
cells.place: in the half-light where the road only shows the next step

cells.tense: Your hand is directing what gets released, and you call the direction the situation.
cells.act: apprentice yourself to the material thing
cells.ask: Pick a plain thing you tend — a plant, a repair, a daily job. Watch what it does for a week without deciding anything for it. Notice what it teaches you about timing.
cells.core:
Something in your life is being carried, tended, and let go of by someone at the table — you. You do it without noise. You set a direction and someone else follows it, and you call that the situation. The person who moved first doesn't appear in the account, and the account is fluent by now.

Next time it runs, hesitate long enough to see it happen. Then take the smaller form of it: tend a plant or a process with fresh hands, learn what it actually needs, ask it for nothing. That's the whole read, no speech required. Your hands are in this, and that's fine.
cells.sheetLine: Your hands are in this, and the story says otherwise.
